bottom_line: In PIONEER AF-PCI, clinically significant bleeding was lower with rivaroxaban-based regimens than with dose-adjusted vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT (group 1 vs. group 3 hazard ratio 0.59 [95% CI, 0.47 to 0.76]; group 2 vs. group 3 hazard ratio 0.63 [95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80]).
implications: These data support that, over 12 months, rivaroxaban-based strategies (group 1: 16.8%; group 2: 18.0%) were associated with lower clinically significant bleeding than vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT (26.7%), with hazard ratios 0.59 (95% CI, 0.47 to 0.76) and 0.63 (95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80). For major adverse cardiovascular events, observed rates were 6.5%, 5.6%, and 6.0% with hazard ratios 1.08 (95% CI, 0.69–1.68) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.59–1.48), and the document states broad confidence intervals and lack of power, so firm conclusions regarding efficacy are not supported by these results.

The primary safety outcome was clinically significant bleeding (a composite of major

criteria or bleeding requiring medical attention).

major_points.text: Clinically significant bleeding at 12 months occurred in 16.8% (group 1), 18.0% (group 2), and 26.7% (group 3), with lower rates in rivaroxaban groups vs standard therapy.
